recommendation: Keep the fix. It restores the non-normative Trial Use status required by FHIR-16371 and later Trial Use decisions without weakening the interoperability rule that supported vital-sign observations conform to the applicable profiles.
issue_request: FHIR-16371 was Published with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification. It objected that normative Observation required use of a non-normative Vital Signs profile; the accepted resolution removed an obsolete note, kept the requirement because it was critical for interoperability, and said the profile should remain non-normative/FMM5.
initial_application: No current git commit explicitly names FHIR-16371. A July 2018 GForge batch commit, 2ebd7c6f7f, removed the stale STU note from observation-vitalsigns-profile-introduction.xml, and current source still retains the SHALL-conform requirement without that note.
additional_context: Later applied issues FHIR-33145, FHIR-39446, and FHIR-39448 reaffirmed that the mandatory Vital Signs profile/page family should be Trial Use. The current active source had drifted back to normative because 9a5f0357ef changed the vital-signs IG and all vital-signs StructureDefinition standards-status values from trial-use to normative in a QA commit without a Jira key.
reconciliation: Changed standards-status metadata from normative to trial-use in source/observation/implementationguide-Observation-vitalsigns.xml and the Vital Signs base/specific StructureDefinition files. The SHALL conformance prose and existing FMM values were left unchanged.
